chunks: Al-Shaykh, may God have mercy on him, narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and 'Ali ibn al-Hakam — both together — from Abu Yahya al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the supererogatory prayer (nafila) during the daytime while traveling. He said: 'O my dear son, if the nafila were valid during travel, the obligatory prayer (farida) would have been complete.'
ai.seo_question: Is the daytime supererogatory prayer (nafila) valid during travel according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Abu Yahya al-Hannat narrates that he asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about performing the supererogatory (nafila) prayer during the daytime while traveling. The Imam's answer — 'O my dear son, if the nafila were valid during travel, the obligatory prayer (farida) would have been complete' — is a concise legal ruling establishing that daytime nafila prayers are not prescribed during travel, grounded in the principle that the farida is itself shortened (qasr) on journey; the validity of the nafila would logically presuppose an unshortened farida.
